    GROBID Server Setup and Administration

    grobid-server-setup.Rmd

    Introduction

    The Get started page presents the quick start for GROBID. This page goes further: it details how to configure, control and monitor the GROBID server used by CheckrefR, whether it runs on your machine (local mode, via Docker) or elsewhere (remote mode).

    It follows the logical order of a working session:

    1. Choose a model: crf or full;
    2. Choose where GROBID runs: locally with grobid_docker_start() (after optionally checking the available versions with grobid_docker_list_versions()), or remotely with grobid_remote_connect();
    3. Check the server status with grobid_server_info();
    4. Stop the local server with grobid_docker_stop();
    5. Save your settings for the session with checkrefr_set_defaults(), and reset them with checkrefr_env_reset().

    Reminder. These functions are not required for everyday use: grobid_process_file() and grobid_process_files() automatically start or join a server based on the mode and model_type arguments. The functions on this page are meant to fine-tune the configuration and to control the server status.

    Choosing a model: crf or full

    GROBID is distributed in two main variants, which differ in the machine learning technique used to analyze documents.

    Model Principle Advantages Constraints
    crf Classical statistical model (Conditional Random Fields) Faster and lighter Generally less accurate
    full Combines the CRF model and neural models (deep learning) Generally more accurate Slower and more resource-intensive (memory, computing time)

    The choice is made with the model_type argument ("crf" or "full"), available in grobid_docker_start(), grobid_remote_connect(), grobid_process_file() and grobid_process_files(). If you do not set it, the behavior depends on the mode:

    • locally, the standard Docker image (without suffix) is used;
    • remotely, the crf demo server is used.

    Learn more. The differences between models, and how to configure them on the GROBID side, are described in the official documentation:

    • GROBID with Docker;
    • Configuration via YAML file;
    • GROBID service.

    Local mode: Docker

    Listing available versions: grobid_docker_list_versions()

    Before choosing a GROBID version, you can list the ones published on Docker Hub, the platform that hosts the images. This function does not require Docker to be installed: it simply queries the website over the Internet.

    versions <- grobid_docker_list_versions(verbose = TRUE)

    The result is a table, sorted from the most recent update to the oldest:

    versions |>
  head(10) |>
  kable_site(caption = "The ten most recent image versions on Docker Hub")

    Data returned by the function

    Column Content
    name Tag name, for example 0.9.0-crf or 0.9.0-full
    full_size Image size, in bytes
    last_updated Date of last update
    digest Unique fingerprint of the image

    Function arguments

    Argument Role Default value
    repository Repository to query (namespace/image) Repository derived from the configured image (lfoppiano/grobid)
    page_size Number of tags requested per page 100
    max_pages Maximum number of pages retrieved 10
    verbose Displays a preview of the first 20 tags TRUE 
    # Query another repository
grobid_docker_list_versions(repository = "grobid/grobid")

    Reading a tag name. Tags follow the form {version}, {version}-crf or {version}-full. The suffix corresponds to the chosen model (see the previous section). The name of the version you select is then passed to the grobid_version argument of grobid_docker_start().

    Starting GROBID locally: grobid_docker_start()

    This function launches GROBID in a Docker container on your machine. It accepts the following settings:

    Argument Role Default value
    model_type Model: "crf" or "full" (see above) not set (standard image)
    grobid_version GROBID version "0.9.0"
    docker_image Base of the Docker image name "lfoppiano/grobid:"
    port Port on your machine on which the service is available 8070
    max_ram Maximum memory allocated to the container (e.g. "4g", "8g", "512m") "4g"
    pull Forces the image download before launching FALSE
    timeout_ready Maximum wait time (seconds) until GROBID is ready 120
    verbose Progress messages TRUE 
    # Start with default settings
grobid_docker_start()
    # Full model, more memory
grobid_docker_start(model_type = "full", max_ram = "8g")

# Specific GROBID version, on another port
grobid_docker_start(grobid_version = "0.8.1", port = 8080)

# Force the image update
grobid_docker_start(pull = TRUE)

    First launch: image download. The first time, the image matching the requested version and model must be downloaded. This can take a while (several GB for the full model). The download is automatic if the image is absent from your machine, even with pull = FALSE. The same download happens for each new version/model combination never used before. The pull = TRUE argument is used to force an update of an image that is already present.

    What the function checks and does for you

    • it checks that Docker is installed and tries to start it if it is not running;
    • it reuses the already active GROBID container if its configuration matches (same image, version, model, port); otherwise, it stops and replaces it;
    • it checks that the requested port is free;
    • it waits for GROBID to respond before returning;
    • it saves the configuration (address, port, version, model) for the session, so that the other functions use it.

    Choosing max_ram. The full model requires more memory. If GROBID stops or fails to start, increase this value, within the limits of what your machine and the Docker configuration (Docker Desktop on Windows and macOS) allow.

    Stopping GROBID locally: grobid_docker_stop()

    When you no longer need the local server, stop it to free up memory and the port.

    grobid_docker_stop()
    Argument Role
    container_id Identifier of a specific container. By default, the one started by grobid_docker_start(); failing that, the function looks for an active GROBID container.
    verbose Progress messages.

    Since the container is launched in “disposable” mode, it is automatically removed when stopped. The function returns TRUE (invisibly) if the container is stopped or was already inactive, and FALSE if no container was identified or if Docker is not running.

    Remote connection preserved. If you are connected to a remote server, stopping a leftover local container does not remove that remote connection: only the configuration related to local mode is reset.

    Remote mode: grobid_remote_connect()

    This function tests and then stores the address of a GROBID server accessible over the Internet. It tries the candidate addresses in order and keeps the first one that responds.

    Demo servers. If no address (url) is provided, CheckrefR uses demo servers hosted on Hugging Face. They are shared, sometimes slow or unavailable, and are not suitable for sensitive or large documents. For regular use, prefer local mode or your own server (url).

    Argument Role Default value
    url Address of your own server. If provided, it is used alone and the demo servers are ignored. NULL
    model_type "crf" or "full": selects the list of demo servers to test. not set (treated as crf)
    timeout Connection timeout in seconds. Each candidate server is tested for at most 120 seconds. 120
    verbose Displays the tested addresses and the result. TRUE 
    # Demo servers, crf model
grobid_remote_connect()

# Demo servers, full model
grobid_remote_connect(model_type = "full")
    # Your own server (recommended without Docker)
grobid_remote_connect(url = "https://my-grobid-server.example.org")

    The demo servers tested by default are:

    urls <- CheckrefR:::.checkrefr_defaults$remote_default_url

data.frame(
  Model  = rep(names(urls), lengths(urls)),
  Server = unlist(urls, use.names = FALSE)
) |>
  kable_site(caption = "Default demo servers")
    Default demo servers
    Model Server
    crf https://grobidorg-grobid.hf.space
    crf https://grobidorg-grobid2.hf.space
    full https://grobidorg-grobid-full.hf.space
    full https://grobidOrg-grobid-full2.hf.space

    The function returns TRUE (invisibly) on success, and stops with an error listing the tested addresses if no server responds. If you are already connected to a remote server that responds, with the same model, the existing connection is simply reused.

    Your own server. You can durably replace (for the session) the demo servers with your own using checkrefr_set_defaults(remote_default_url = ...) (see below). That way, grobid_remote_connect() and the processing functions will use your servers without having to repeat the address.

    Monitoring the server: grobid_server_info()

    This function displays the status of the currently configured server: mode, address, reachability and version.

    info <- grobid_server_info()
#> 
#> ── GROBID Server ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Mode: not configured
#> URL: -
#> Reachable: no
#> Version: unknown
#> Timeout: -

    The result is also returned (invisibly) as a list:

    Element Content
    mode "docker", "remote" or "not configured"
    url Server address, or NA
    api_reachable TRUE if the server responds
    grobid_version GROBID version returned by the server, otherwise NA
    timeout Timeout used for the test, otherwise NA 
    str(info)
#> List of 5
#>  $ mode          : chr "not configured"
#>  $ url           : chr NA
#>  $ api_reachable : logi FALSE
#>  $ grobid_version: chr NA
#>  $ timeout       : int NA

    No server configured. If no server has been started or joined yet, the function makes no connection and returns mode = "not configured". This is the normal case at the start of a session, before any call to grobid_docker_start(), grobid_remote_connect() or the processing functions.

    An example of a complete sequence, in local mode:

    grobid_docker_start(model_type = "crf")
grobid_server_info()   # "docker" mode, server reachable
grobid_docker_stop()
grobid_server_info()   # back to "not configured"

    Configuring your settings: checkrefr_set_defaults()

    Rather than repeating the same arguments in every call, checkrefr_set_defaults() lets you change the package’s default values for the current session: GROBID version, port, timeouts, number of parallel processes, validation thresholds and weights, remote server addresses, etc.

    Scope of the settings. They are kept only for the current R session. They are not saved to disk: when R is restarted, the original values are restored. To keep your settings from one session to the next, place the calls to checkrefr_set_defaults() in your startup script (or in your .Rprofile file).

    # A single default GROBID version, a shorter timeout
# and two parallel processes
checkrefr_set_defaults(
  grobid_version = "0.8.1",
  timeout        = 60L,
  max_workers    = 2L
)

    The function displays the modified parameters. Called without arguments, it applies no change and invites you to check the current state.

    Modifiable parameters

    Connection and GROBID server

    Parameter Role Initial value
    docker_image Base of the Docker image name "lfoppiano/grobid:"
    grobid_version GROBID version "0.9.0"
    grobid_model_type Default model ("crf", "full" or NA) NA
    docker_port Local port used in Docker mode "8070"
    remote_default_url Default remote servers (crf and full lists) demo servers
    timeout Connection timeout, in seconds 120
    max_workers Number of parallel processes for grobid_process_files() 4
    grobid_email E-mail address associated with requests NA

    Protected parameters. The elements that describe the current state of the server (mode, server_url, docker_container_id) and the identity of the package (pkg_name, pkg_repo) cannot be modified with this function. They are managed automatically by grobid_docker_start(), grobid_remote_connect() and grobid_docker_stop().

    # Credentials for OpenAlex and DOI services
checkrefr_set_defaults(
  oa_api_key = "my_api_key",
  doi_email  = "me@example.com"
)

    Declaring your own remote servers

    For remote_default_url, you provide a named list with the keys crf and/or full. The addresses provided are merged with the existing list (duplicates are removed):

    • a simple vector of addresses appends them to the end of the list;
    • a list named by ranks ("1", "2", …) inserts them at the indicated position; rank 1 places the address first, so it is tested before the demo servers.
    # Your server tested first for the full model
checkrefr_set_defaults(
  remote_default_url = list(
    full = list("1" = "https://my-server.example.com")
  )
)

# Append to the end of the crf model list
checkrefr_set_defaults(
  remote_default_url = list(
    crf = "https://my-other-server.example.com"
  )
)

    Resetting your settings: checkrefr_env_reset()

    To return to the package’s original values, use checkrefr_env_reset().

    Argument Role Default value
    fields Names of the parameters to reset. NULL: full reset. NULL
    verbose Displays messages. TRUE

    Partial reset: only the named parameters return to their original value.

    checkrefr_set_defaults(timeout = 30L, oa_min_threshold = 0.55)
#> ✔ Variable(s) updated: "timeout" and "oa_min_threshold"

checkrefr_env_reset(fields = c("timeout", "oa_min_threshold"))
#> ✔ Parameter(s) reset: "timeout" and "oa_min_threshold"

    An unknown parameter name is ignored with a warning, while the other names are still reset:

    checkrefr_env_reset(fields = c("timeout", "nonexistent_variable"))

    Full reset: all parameters return to their original value.

    checkrefr_env_reset()

    Full reset and server state. The full reset also clears the server state (mode, address, container identifier). If a local GROBID container is still active, the package no longer “knows” about it: stop it beforehand with grobid_docker_stop(), otherwise it will keep running in the background. However, grobid_docker_stop() is able to find an active GROBID container even without a stored identifier.

    The function invisibly returns the package’s internal environment; its normal use is limited to the messages displayed.

    Summary

    Need Function
    Find out which image versions are available grobid_docker_list_versions()
    Start GROBID locally and set version, model, port, memory grobid_docker_start()
    Connect to a remote server, or to your own server grobid_remote_connect()
    Check the status of the configured server grobid_server_info()
    Stop the local server grobid_docker_stop()
    Change the default values for the session checkrefr_set_defaults()
    Return to the original values checkrefr_env_reset()
